description: In this UCF Remembers 9/11 interview, the speaker recalls being 21 and working at a restaurant when television screens showed coverage of the September 11 attacks. The speaker describes watching the coverage at work, including footage of the attacks in New York, Pennsylvania, and at the Pentagon, and the collapse of a Trade Center building. The speaker recalls feeling shocked and frightened, and later connecting anxiety and panic attacks to watching repeated television coverage of people dying. After completing an AA degree and coming to UCF, the speaker describes using counseling services to explore the effects of the experience. The speaker says a later visit to the New York memorial, during a conference visit that year, was healing in some ways; this account describes a visit to the memorial, not presence at an attack site on September 11. The interview metadata gives a recording date of September 11, 2026, distinct from the collection's identification of the September 11 terrorist attacks as the 2001 event.
